reason: The cited handler fills elements on the current browser page with caller-supplied values, which can deliver agent-supplied data into a webpage context, so SINK is supported. It can optionally call response.includeSnapshot(), which indicates returning a page snapshot; browser page content may contain user-private data and is also attacker-controllable web content, so SECRET and UNTRUSTED are supported. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution; interacting with/filling a browser page is not HOSTEXEC.
